div.head: Ine 76.3
div.ab: Gif hit biscepsunu sie, sie be healfum þam.
Gif hit biscopsunu sy, sy be healfum þam seo bote.
Gyf hit bisceopsunu sy, sy be healfum ðem.
Si episcopi fili(ol)us sit, sit dimidium hoc.
Gif hit biscepsunu sie, sie be healfum þam.
Gif hit bisceopsunu sie, \sie/ be healfum þam.
Wenn es [der Erschlagene] ein Firm-Pathenkind ist, sei (die Busseneinnahme) halb [so viel wie] die [vom Taufpathen].
If it [the slain man] is a confirmation-godchild, let (the compensation) be half [as much as] that [for a baptismal godchild].
In the case of the godson of a bishop, [the sum] shall be half [the amount paid for the godson of a king].
If it is a spiritual son at confirmation, the compensation is to be half as much.
If [the slain person] is a bishop’s [god]son, let [the compensation] be half [that for a king’s godson].

Nicht ‘Bischofs [!] Sohn’ (ein Irrtum, der als zölibatswidrig die Leges Angl. Lond., auch laut Hs. Rs, um 1200 veranlasste, 76, 3 fortzulassen) oder ‘Bischofs Taufsohn’. Nur der Bischof (s. d. Gl 5 b) darf firmeln; vgl. Toller, auch Suppl. s. v. bisceopian (= geb∼): ‘firmeln’ (s. d. Gl), unbiscpod ‘ungefirmelt’, bisceopung ‘Firmelung’ [auch Nord. biskupa]; das Verb lebt bis zur Neuzeit allgemein, jetzt noch dialektisch (Wright Dial. dict. s. v. bishop). Ælfred, der spätere König, ward a. 853 von Papst Leo IV. laut dessen Briefes zum spiritalis filius genommen (hiene to biscepsunu nam; Ann. Agsax. = in filium adoptionis confirma[tus]; Asser = filium a chrismate nominavit, ut modo sub manu episcopi solemus accipientes parvulos filios nominare; Ethelwerd 510 D. Æthelnoth (später Erzb. von Canterbury) salbte König Cnut mit Chrisma; Osbern Transl. s. Ælfegi

Not ‘bishop’s [!] son’ (an error which, as contrary to celibacy, caused the Leges Angl. Lond., also according to MS Rs, c. 1200, to omit 76, 3) or ‘bishop’s godson’. Only the bishop (see that word in Gl 5 b) may confirm; cf. Toller, also Suppl. s. v. bisceopian (= geb∼): ‘confirm’ (see that word in Gl), unbiscpod ‘unconfirmed’, bisceopung ‘confirmation’ [also Norse biskupa]; the verb lived on in general use into modern times and still survives in dialect (Wright Dial. dict. s. v. bishop). Ælfred, the later king, was taken by Pope Leo IV in 853 as his spiritalis filius, according to the latter’s letter (hiene to biscepsunu nam; Ann. Agsax. = in filium adoptionis confirma[tus]; Asser = filium a chrismate nominavit, ut modo sub manu episcopi solemus accipientes parvulos filios nominare; Ethelwerd 510 D. Æthelnoth (later Archbishop of Canterbury) anointed King Cnut with chrism; Osbern Transl. s. Ælfegi
H’s Ergänzung ist laut unorgan. -e spät.
H’s supplement is late, as the inorganic -e shows.
Taufe gilt also wichtiger als Firmelung. Vgl. Gt Taufverwandte 3. — Nur in hbq folgt Blas hinter Ine nur in H so, als wäre es ein Stück davon
Baptism is thus regarded as more important than confirmation. Cf. Gt Taufverwandte 3. — Only in hbq does Blas follow after Ine; only in H in such a way as if it were a part of it
